uncited: It builds on [Intersection using Rasterization](8072-intersection-using-rasterization.md) by using two rendering passes to decouple the calculation of ray entry/exit points from the volumetric integration.
The method requires two rendering passes.
The first pass calculates the exit point of the ray.
*   **Volume Data:** A 3D texture (`volume`) containing the scalar field.
**Initialization:** Create and compile vertex and fragment shaders.
Pass the Model-View-Projection matrix, camera position, and step size.
**Second Pass Rendering:** Draw the unit cube using the 36 indices.
*   **Step Size (`h`):** Determines the resolution of the ray march.
A smaller `h` increases accuracy but reduces performance.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of samples per ray ($N$) and the number of pixels ($P$). $O(P \times N)$.
The method originated from the need to perform volume rendering on programmable graphics hardware.
